ARTEFACT: Αy type of archaeological find, regardless of size. Annotate adjectives together with the ARTEFACT only when they form a single unified concept (e.g., «οικιακό σκεύος» – “domestic vessel”; «αναθηματική στήλη» – “ votive stele”). However, adjectives indicating material (e.g., «μεταλλικό» εργαλείο – “metal” tool) or a chronological period (e.g «γεωμετρικός» αμφορέας – “geometric” amphora) must be annotated separately as MATERIAL and PERIOD entities respectively. This entity includes architectural members of buildings when they occur as detached, movable individual elements of a structure (e.g., τμήματα ἀπὸ τὸν κατεστραμμένο «θριγκὸ» – parts of the destroyed “entablature”). Distinguish when a material constitutes an ARTEFACT and when it is the material of an ARTEFACT. For example, bones as finds in a grave belong to ARTEFACT, whereas bones as the material of another object (e.g., «οστέινο» εργαλείο – “bone” tool) are annotated as MATERIAL. Objects represented in iconographic scenes and reliefs (e.g., jewelry, weapons, furniture) are annotated as ARTEFACT. Literary works, inscriptions, and every type of alphabet are annotated as ARTEFACT, e.g., Ἡ «ἐπιγραφή», ἀποτελούμενη ἀπὸ «συλλαβογράμματα» τῆς «Γραμμικῆς Α γραφῆς» καὶ ἕνα «ἰδεόγραμμα» (The “inscription”, consisting of “syllabograms” of the “Linear A script” and an “ideogram”).
PERIOD:
Αrchaeological periods and dates. E.g., «βυζαντινός» ναός, «προϊστορικός» οικισμός του Θορικού (“Byzantine” church; “prehistoric” settlement of Thorikos). Do not annotate modern-era periods and dates.
Exclude prefixes like “until" (μέχρι), “about/approximately” (περίπου); annotate only the period. Annotate surrounding words for multi-year spans. E.g., «από τον 2ο μέχρι το τέλος του 6ου αι. μ.Χ.» (“from the 2nd until the end of the 6th c. AD”), «στη διάρκεια τοῦ 1ου αἰ. π.Χ» (“during the 1st c. BC”). Annotate entire period names. E.g., «νεότερη νεολιθική περίοδος» (“Late Neolithic period”). Period abbreviations are annotated as a single span (e.g., «ΥΕ ΙΙΙΒ/Γ» – “LH IIIB/C”). When a chronological period is followed by an explanatory date range in parentheses, the period and the explanation are annotated separately (e.g., «Πρωτοελλαδικής και Μεσοελλαδικής περιόδου» («3200/3000–1600 π.Χ.» – “Early Helladic and Middle Helladic periods” (“3200/3000–1600 BC”). Do not annotate indefinite periods, such as σε αὐτὴ τὴν περίοδο (this period).
LOCATION: cities, villages, locations, countries, rivers, seas, etc. Do not include very general concepts (e.g., οικισμός – settlement, αιγιαλίτιδα ζώνη – coastal zone). The term settlement is not annotated unless accompanied by a modifier (e.g., Ο ΠΡΟΪΣΤΟΡΙΚΟΣ «ΟΙΚΙΣΜΟΣ ΤΟΥ ΘΟΡΙΚΟΥ» – THE PREHISTORIC “SETTLEMENT OF THORIKOS”). Annotate places such as «Αρχαιολογικό Μουσείο Ιωαννίνων» (“Archaeological Museum of Ioannina”). Directions are not included in the annotation (e.g., βόρειο τμήμα του τεμένους – northern part of the sanctuary), nor are adjectives denoting origin (e.g., αιγύπτιου «ναοφόρου» – of an Egyptian “naophoros”). Pay attention to the meaning of the sentence. For example: “The scene of the Ascension of Alexander was particularly popular, from as early as the 10th century, in the Byzantine world and beyond”: here, «Βυζαντινό κόσμο» (“Byzantine world”) is tagged as LOCATION. In the phrase: «χάλκινες κοπὲς Κορίνθου» (“bronze mints of Corinth”), the reference is to Corinthian coinage (ARTΕFACT), not to the city of Corinth. Cities and countries are annotated as separate entities (e.g., «Darmstadt» «Γερμανίας» – “Darmstadt” in “Germany”). To avoid ambiguity arising from toponymic homonymy, villages are annotated together with their province or district as a single entity, e.g., «Ακρωτήρι Θήρας» (“Akrotiri of Thera”); «Ζάβαλι» «Λαδοχωρίου Ηγουμενίτσας» (“Zavali”, “Ladochori of Igoumenitsa”).
CONTEXT:
stratigraphic units of an archaeological site that contain finds 
buildings and anthropogenic constructions that are not finds (ARTΕFACTS), but may contain finds
It includes architectural structures and immovable constructions in situ, e.g., temples, wells, walls, etc. (Detached parts of a monument belong to the category ARTEFACT, e.g., τμήμα «επιτύμβιας στήλης» (a fragment of a “funerary stele”).
Do not annotate modern interventions, such as «ανασκαφικές τομές» (excavation trenches).
Overly general contexts such as κτίριο (building), μνημείο (monument), οικοδόμημα (edifice), οικισμός (settlement) are not tagged, unless accompanied by an adjective or further specification.
 Shapes are not annotated, e.g., ημικυκλική «κόγχη» (“semicircular niche”); «ορθογώνιος λάκκος» (rectangular “pit”). An exception applies when the shape defines an architectural ground plan, e.g., «κτιρίων ορθογώνιας κάτοψης» (“buildings of rectangular plan”); λείψανα «κυκλικών κατασκευών» (“remains of circular structures”). 
Conventional names such as «βόρεια βασιλική» (“North Basilica”) are included, but not adjectives denoting orientation, e.g., στον νότιο «τοίχο» (in the south “wall”). 
Monuments dedicated to a saint or god are annotated as CONTEXT (e.g., «ναοῦ τοῦ Ἐπικουρίου Ἀπόλλωνος» – “temple of Apollo Epikourios”). The name of the saint/god is not annotated as PERSON.
Parts of a citiy (acropolis, agora, cemetery) belong to this category. Ε.g., ὅριζαν τὴ δυτικὴ πλευρὰ τῆς «ἀγορᾶς» τῆς πόλης (they defined the western side of the city’s “agora”).
MATERIAL: Materials from which a find (ARTEFACT) or architectural member (CONTEXT) is made. Do not annotate adjectives defining materials. Ε.g., λευκό «μάρμαρο» (white “marble”); «αποκρουσμένο λίθο» (chipped “stone”). Do not annotate very general terms, e.g., αλλόχθονες πρώτες ύλες (allochthonous raw materials). Older architectural parts are annotated when reused as building materials (spolia), e.g., «αρχαία αρχιτεκτονικά μέλη» (“ancient architectural members”) used intact or with minimal hewing.
SPECIES: Animal and plant species. Ε.g., «Αγελάδα» προς τα δεξιά, θηλάζει το «μοσχαράκι» της (“Cow” to the right, suckling her “calf”). When a species (e.g., a shell) constitutes the material of an object, it is annotated as MATERIAL; for example, jewelry made of «Spondylus gaederopus». Mythological creatures such as gryphons are included under SPECIES. Mythological beings that speak or act as persons, such as the Sphinx, are annotated as PERSON.
PERSON: Historical or mythological figures. Do not annotate individuals living in the modern era.
FEATURE: stylistic, typological and iconographic characteristics. Do not annotate all descriptive adjectives, only terms that indicate: construction techniques (e.g., «ισοδομικό σύστημα» – “isodomic masonry”; «ψηφιδωτό» – “mosaic”), architectural or painting styles («δικιόνιος σταυροειδής εγγεγραμμένος» ναός – “two-column cross-in-square” church; «ερυθρόμορφο» αγγείο – “red-figure” vase), iconographic themes (e.g., «Ανάληψη του Αλεξάνδρου» – “Ascension of Alexander”; «ένθρονη μορφή» – “enthroned figure”; «Πρόμαχος» – “Promachos”), and artistic trends (e.g., «αιγυπτιάζοντα» αγάλματα – “Egyptianizing” statues). The term «βυζαντινός» (“Byzantine”) is annotated primarily as PERIOD (not FEATURE). Annotate different types of decoration («ανάγλυφη διακόσμηση» – “relief decoration”; «φυτική διακόσμηση» – “floral decoration”; «ενεπίγραφη διακόσμηση» – “inscribed decoration”) without including further details (e.g., «φυτικὴ διακόσμηση» ἀπὸ φύλλο κισσοῦ – “floral decoration” of ivy leaf). Individual iconographic elements of a decoration can be annotated as ARTEFACT (e.g., holding a «τύμπανο» – “drum” with the left hand and a «φιάλη» – “phiale” with the right). This category also includes types of figurines and statues, e.g., «ανθρωπόμορφα και ζωόμορφα» ειδώλια (“anthropomorphic and zoomorphic figurines”); «ιερακόμορφο» ειδώλιο (“falcon-shaped” figurine); «κούροι» (“kouroi”).
